name: Gavar
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Viljoen, Melanie H. (comp.). 2022. Gavar expository texts collection. SIL Language and Culture Archives. 20 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Interlinear tone-marked texts only; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Viljoen, Melanie. 2017. The Gavar Verb Phrase. Yaounde: SIL / Ministry of Scientific Research and Innovation. 108 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; the word 'stress' does not occur. Sec. 2.3 'Tone on verb roots' (pp.13-14) and Appendix A: verb roots underlyingly toneless, default surface tone mid, depressor and raiser consonants, H/L tone spreading from prefixes.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard. 2014. The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic. LOT Dissertation Series 375. Utrecht: LOT.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 5.3.2 Daba group: Gavar (data from Noukeu 2004) has lost vowel prosodies, four vowels /a ə i e/, /s/ vs /ʃ/ contrast; the reconstruction explicitly excludes tone and stress; nothing on Gavar stress.

sources.citation: Viljoen, Melanie Helen. 2013. A Grammatical Description of the Buwal Language. PhD thesis, La Trobe University. doi:10.26181/21845661.v1 (Buwal, buwa1243, Gavar's closest relative)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Describes Buwal, not Gavar. Sec. 1.1.4 'Linguistic relationship with Gavar' and scattered comparative notes (author's Gavar fieldnotes) contain nothing on Gavar prosody; for Buwal itself ch. 2 treats tone only and p.87 remarks that Chadic metrical structure 'is not stress (as normally understood in terms of higher pitch or intensity) but has to do with syllable weight', with no such interaction found in Buwal. No Gavar stress statement.

sources.citation: Viljoen, Melanie H. 2009. Precis d'orthographe pour la langue gavar. Edition preliminaire. Yaounde: SIL Cameroun. 37 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2 gives consonant/vowel inventories and syllable rules; sec. 3 'Les tons' (p.13) states three surface tones (haut, moyen, bas), lexical tone not. the only 'accent' in the document is 'accent aigu' (the diacritic chosen for the 3PL subject pronoun). No word on stress/accent as prominence.

sources.citation: Seguin, Lawrence Marc. 1992. Enquete sociolinguistique sur le gavar (enquete preliminaire). Yaounde: SIL. 8 pp. (image scan; scanned here)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey (location, classification, bilingualism); no phonology, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Wolff, H. Ekkehard. 2022. A Historical Phonology of Central Chadic: Prosodies and Lexical Reconstruction. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: Language-by-language treatment of all Central Chadic languages including the Daba group (Gavar); its prosody sections may summarise what Noukeu 2004 / Viljoen say about Gavar suprasegmentals (second-hand at best).

sources.citation: Viljoen, Melanie. 2019. Gavar verb morphology. In Ibriszimow, Tourneux & Wolff (eds.), Topics in Chadic Linguistics X (Chadic Linguistics / Linguistique tchadique / Tschadistik). Cologne: Ruediger Koeppe.

sources.note: The only dedicated phonological description of Gavar (Glottolog listed by Glottolog as a phonology; data source for Gravina 2014); a Yaounde I phonology memoire normally has a 'traits suprasegmentaux' chapter (tons, accent) and is the one place a first-hand stress/accent statement would be.
